01 / THE DEFINING DECISION

Precision supplies tension. Decoration releases it.

The player chooses where to remove material, which tool can reach a shoulder, and when further work is more dangerous than useful. Painting then turns a constrained task into authorship.

01 / ORDERRead a silhouette and its offer.
02 / CARVETrade fast removal for local control.
03 / FINISHSand; paint; reveal a pattern.
04 / EVALUATECompare shape and collect cash.
05 / REINVESTChoose workshop progress or a collection unlock.

The target line carries two messages: what the object should become and how much material remains safe to remove. The tool footprint mediates both. A broad edge clears a shaft efficiently; a small edge can address a neck without taking the neighbouring shoulder with it. This is a spatial judgment loop, rather than a timed reflex challenge.

The source presents both a clean, abstract crafting interface and a customer-facing workshop. Their state sequences overlap, but their tool trays, rewards and progression should remain separate. The mobile web target can deliberately combine the workshop's continuity with the earlier interface's generous decoration choices.

Design implication: keep the contour, cutting edge and untouched wood readable together. Every meaningful drag should explain its consequence before a final accuracy meter does.

02 / TOOL → MATERIAL → OBJECT

The same object carries the work forward.

Each stage changes the action vocabulary while preserving the player's artifact. The value of the sequence comes from seeing earlier choices survive into the finish.

Teach at the point of contact

A hand tracing an infinity gesture invites a drag directly on the blank. There is little abstraction between the instruction and the desired outcome: the tool is already present, the contour is already present, and the next meaningful action is physical.

Yet a gesture alone cannot teach tool width or safe depth. Watching chips is satisfying; understanding why a shoulder vanished is what produces skill. A target adaptation should reveal the active footprint before contact and leave a visible record of undercut areas afterwards.

Chisel selection is a geometry choice. Shop handles and slot positions are weaker evidence of function; a green handle should not automatically mean greater precision or cutting power.

Sanding narrows the gesture, not the responsibility

The sponge replaces the chisel and introduces a size slider. The interface is teaching a second kind of control: contact coverage rather than aggressive cutting. Smoothing and restoring missing material are different operations. The visible slider proves an adjustable tool surface, but not a mesh algorithm or a guaranteed rescue from overcutting.

Finish with freedom and a reveal

Colour can be laid along the object's axis, making bands that read around a turned form. Patterning creates a second reveal: the craft is already recognisable, but uncovering the finish makes it feel completed. Decals add a final focal mark without requiring a new object.

A good adaptation keeps subtraction consequential and decoration permissive. It gives each stage a distinct feel without turning finishing into automatic repair.
03 / SCORE, REWARD & INTERRUPTION

The final number is feedback—and a spending invitation.

The completed object earns a score and currency. Video offers sit beside that reward, and can also sit inside the tool and recovery choices.

This paired reading matters: an intermediate number is not a separate reward tier. An offer of 260 and a stable payout of 300 also do not establish a universal percentage bonus. The valuation formula, decoration contribution and score tolerance remain unverified.

The earlier results distinguish precision numerically while maintaining a celebratory tone. That can support a relaxed craft fantasy, but a near-perfect number alone does not teach which area deserves another pass. A live local error signal would answer a more useful question: where should I work, and when should I stop?

Source ads participate in the loop

Video icons appear on tool unlocks, REPAIR, reward multiplication and additional chest openings. They therefore gate convenience, expressive choice and reward intensity in different places. The visible controls do not establish every ad's completion behavior or the frequency of interstitials.

The chest grid adds a random-looking reward interruption between craft jobs. Three opened values are visible; the underlying distribution and opening allowance require temporal evidence. It contributes little to learning precision.

Target decision: the complete craft loop remains free. Remove ad-dependent repairs and multipliers, give all necessary cutting profiles from the start, and use earned cash for visible workshop and style progression.

04 / A SESSION NEEDS A REASON TO CONTINUE

Spend on the bench, the tools—or the next object.

Currency ties individual jobs together. The strongest proof of progression is a matched workshop purchase, where cash, counter and environment change together.

That purchase closes a causal chain: completed jobs produce cash; expenditure changes the workspace; the counter and next price make another purchase legible. Its effect on pay, cutting physics or order availability is not established, so the target should treat workshop improvement as visual progression unless it deliberately defines another benefit.

Complexity changes the cutting problem

Broad umbrella spans, bottle necks, cone tapers and a multi-tier cake ask for different tool paths. Novelty is strongest when a new outline introduces a new spatial problem, rather than simply reskinning the same cylinder.

The workshop also exposes a 315 offer and BEST OFFER control. A later trophy result reads 99% and 538. Those states support the presence of different reward magnitudes; they do not prove that repeated skipping always increases pay or that workshop level causes premium orders.

A web adaptation should make commissions openly selectable by complexity, keep difficult shapes reachable, and preserve an endless mastery loop after its authored workshop milestones.

Alternative dispatch is a choice surface

The clean-background version shows four silhouettes with quoted coin amounts. It lets the next artifact itself become the reason to continue. That is a stronger fit for a calm craft game than forcing a player through an escalating negotiation routine.

The target blends the two deliberately: a customer brief provides context, a small commission list provides choice, and the chosen silhouette defines the next blank.

05 / DEVELOPMENT, AUDIENCE & RECEPTION

A durable mobile promise, with version-sensitive evidence.

The commercial promise is easy to understand: a tactile craft, an attractive object and a room that grows with repeated work. Popularity does not resolve the rules of a particular recorded build.

Voodoo is the named mobile developer/seller. The current listings describe customer orders, carving, polishing, painting and room upgrades. The two recorded interfaces are compatible with iteration around that promise, but their build numbers are not visible. The original engine, individual development team, production budget and revenue are unverified.

Historical feedback becomes a test question

Three dated App Store reviews from March–April 2020 describe calming craft, difficult tool reach at corners, and workshop clutter or weak functional upgrades. They are individual anecdotes. Later version notes mention performance and reliability, but do not document fixes for those particular problems. Dated player feedback and version history.

Reported problemDocumented change / applicabilityTarget regression question
Tools cannot comfortably reach narrow ends or corners.No specific shipped fix verified; recorded tray changes do not prove reachable geometry.Can every authored shoulder and candle be completed using the three free profiles on a phone?
Workshop scenery competes with the working object.The workshop interface is visible; causal readability improvement remains unmeasured.Do the outline, tool edge and chips remain distinguishable over the background during contact?
Upgrades feel cosmetic rather than functional.A visible bench change is checked; performance effects are unknown.Is each target upgrade honestly described and visibly applied, without an unsupported promise of precision or pay?

The likely audience is players seeking short, low-pressure tactile creation. That is a positioning inference from the product and repeated craft structure, not a measured demographic. The best web adaptation should respect both motives: relaxing expression and improving hand control. It should avoid noisy prompts that interrupt the action whose satisfaction brings the player back.

Do not ship a demo in place of this complete game; do not publish without a separate publication request.

Complete target scope · Designed

Working identity: an original cosy lathe workshop, single player, portrait-first, touch and mouse. A player accepts a commission, removes wood using a selected profile, sands locally, paints and reveals a finish, adds an optional decal, gets an honest shape result and cash, and chooses another job or a visible upgrade. No mandatory timers, lives, stamina, ads, platform coins or purchases govern the craft.

Whole content structure: author fifteen profile families inspired by observed craft problems: arrow, umbrella, potion bottle, rocket, traffic cone, ice cream, plunger, dumbbell, money bag, vase, rounded phone-like token, wine bottle, rattle, goblet/trophy and stepped birthday cake. Implement all fifteen families. Use rotationally feasible approximations, particularly the phone-like token. Give each two designed proportion variants, for thirty playable commissions. Unlock all shapes within ordinary workshop progression; after milestone 10, offer endless shuffled commissions with repeat/mastery/galleries, not a locked ending. No source maximum or ending is claimed.

Progression: three functional profiles—broad flat, rounded gouge, narrow point—are free from job one. First commission is a simple arrow. Begin with six basic colours plus a free neutral timber finish, three simple patterns and three original decals. Earned soft cash adds six more colours, three patterns, six decals and cosmetic tool handles; all are part of the complete free base. Ten workshop milestones visibly change supports, mat, storage, lighting and display shelf. Cosmetic handles and room upgrades have no hidden cutting-stat advantage.

Balance starting proposal: first clean arrow earns 300 soft cash; small/medium/complex jobs quote 300/360/540 maximum. Set payout to rounded quoted maximum×final shape accuracy, with a 30% completion floor so errors do not halt progression. First workshop costs 500, next 578, next 668; remaining seven costs are a designed smooth rising curve, initially 780,900, 1040, 1200, 1380, 1590, 1830. Style unlocks cost 200 each; all functional tools stay free. Validate the rate in normal play: second successful simple job can afford milestone 1; thirty commissions and repeated mastery can fund the full collection. These constants intentionally do not certify either source economy.

Save scope: completed-job ledger, cash, collection ownership, workshop milestone, gallery recipes and unlocked commissions persist. Persist in-progress profile, paint, mask and decal recipe at meaningful checkpoints; resume the same job after reload. Keep settings in a separate key. Add a clearly explained new-save control with confirmation in Settings, not beside the cutting tool. Keep up to 30 gallery recipes, letting the player replace an old one deliberately; procedural recipes are enough to rebuild images.

Difficulty and freedom: preserve small shoulders, narrow necks and layered cake features. Gradually present them, but never require a purchased tool to reach a profile. Sanding cannot restore missing radius. Decoration may be skipped or left bare, without reducing geometric score. A bad shape can still be completed, kept, retried from a fresh blank or followed by another job. There is no mandatory perfect-score gate.

Design space: build an efficient original renderer and tactile input model, choose a fair accuracy formula and tune its tolerance through the cases below. Create original customer silhouettes, object variations, workshop art, materials and sound. Do not copy creator overlays, source characters, brand marks or screenshot textures as game assets.

Core statements to preserve

  1. Removal is spatial. A drag changes the radius where its active cutting edge actually contacts the blank; untouched regions retain their geometry. A full-width automatic reveal is not a cut.
  2. Tool footprint changes the route. Broad, rounded and pointed profiles make different traces from the same input. A narrow shoulder must be reachable with a free profile.
  3. Stopping matters. Crossing inside the target removes wanted material. The contour never silently clamps the tool to success.
  4. Finishing carries history. Sanding smooths local roughness by removal; paint and masks change surfaces; none fills a deep cut.
  5. Appearance belongs to the player. Colour bands, patterns and decals compose on the player's actual shape, not a replacement perfect model.
  6. Score explains geometry. Live preview and final score use the same shape inputs; undercuts remain visible and cannot become perfect because a stencil was peeled.
  7. Cash has a visible destination. A completed job credits once; a workshop/style purchase debits once and makes a persistent change.
  8. The next object changes the task. Variety includes tapers, coves, steps and small preserved features; every commission remains reachable in the free base.

Local-library pilot · completed, one transfer accepted

The local teardown archive was available. The pilot addressed two concrete problems: recognising an irreversible cut boundary, and understanding the first effective tool contact. Read-only queries were drag cut precision overcut irreversible silhouette feedback and tool contact first touch immediate feedback shaping painting.

First shortlist: Attack Hole, Mr Ninja, Paper.io 2, Slice It All!; these did not give a close continuous profile-control solution. Second shortlist: Sculpt People, Tie Dye, Cut and Paint, Slice It All!. Sculpt People's first-real-job teaching in §§02–03 and the embedded fig-lathe-infinity/fig-carve-praise were read/extracted and visually inspected. Accepted only the once-only contact guide; rejected unlimited deformation and guaranteed praise. Slice It All!'s timing/flip loop was rejected as a different input problem. Tie Dye and Cut and Paint share the craft/reveal vocabulary but supplied no stronger solution to irreversible radial precision; no additional transfer was selected.

Before/after hypothesis: an unaided first blank leaves a novice searching for the action; a brief guide makes first effective contact legible without an instruction page. Risk: the guide can encourage deep repeated strokes. Show a short safe outer path, remove it on actual contact, and never apply hidden cuts. Check: on a normal phone, a new player makes the first cut without opening help, recognises that the contour is a stopping reference, and can repeat independently on job two. No measured retention uplift or donor art reuse is claimed.

Roblox analog · one relevant transfer

Bloom Brain available locally. No search_kb MCP was exposed; bundled scripts/locate_bloom_brain.py --query located a 619-page knowledge base, and its local keyword search was used. Queries: woodturning sculpt carve crafting tool shape building first action feedback; satisfying destroy remove material drag cut visible upgrade workshop.

The close candidate was Carve Wood!, local artifacts/pages/carve-wood.md, report dated 03 Sep 2026, capture dated 02 Sep 2026. Its inspected text describes one-finger carving against an outline, Standard/Wedge/Circular profiles, no undo, and live accuracy plus projected price on each stroke. The source KB images were not available locally; textual evidence was inspected, without claiming to have viewed those screenshots. Universe 10404519332 / place 82712304391069 identify the analog, not the target.

Accepted / Designed: a small live score and expected payout, paired with a coloured local undercut indication, answers when to stop. Target reward preview is transparent and settles with the same calculation. Mechanism: shortening the delay from cut to useful evaluation lets the player learn tool width/depth. Risk: score watching can crowd out craft; keep the preview quiet and leave decoration score-neutral. Validation: complete ten normal phone carves with shallow mistakes, deep mistakes and intact corners; preview must agree with final settlement and highlight the location of damage without hiding the outline.

Other candidates included Wash House and Unbox ASMR. Wash House's repeated object-count/co-op structure is a weaker fit for local precision; no second transfer selected. Tycoon forestry, automation, server visits, RNG seeds, Robux gates and compulsory daily rewards are excluded. Their popularity would not establish a causal benefit for this craft.

Around 2 minutesKeep the first painted artifact and see cash settle.One complete short target loop; tune normal play, do not fast-forward the test.
Around 5 minutesTry a different profile family and a style choice.Tool geometry + commission novelty. Every free profile has a useful role.
Around 10 minutesChoose a visible workshop milestone or collection colour.Checked source spend loop; target costs Designed. No extra prompt after an error.
Around 20 minutesAttempt a layered cake, compare earlier artifact, and replay for mastery.Cake complexity + designed gallery/endless loop. No claimed engagement uplift.
Target controls, geometry, UI and feel contract
IDDesigned behaviorAcceptance boundary
D01 · inputOne pointer drags an offset tool tip; pointer capture maintains contact until up/cancel. Touch camera fixed during cutting; drag outside canvas never scrolls the page. Keep tip above finger with adjustable left/right bias. Mouse works identically.Pointer up, cancel, window blur and platform pause release contact and sound. Multi-touch cannot create an extra cut. UI taps never cut the blank.
D02 · profile modelRepresent radius along an axis as a sufficiently dense sampled profile or equivalent original mesh. Tool shape subtracts only at actual overlap; interpolation prevents gaps on fast strokes. Keep untargeted material unchanged.Same path produces comparable removal at 30/60/120 fps. Do not accumulate deep cuts merely because a stationary touch sits on the surface; pressure/depth must remain legible.
D03 · danger / stopOutline remains visible over the working surface; broad/round/point footprints preview. Under-target radii get a quiet damage tint; no outline snap and no invisible auto-completion.Undercut persists through sanding/paint and lowers geometric score. Deep error gets free whole-job reset or completion choices, not a repair purchase.
D04 · sandingSponge size changes contact width. Local ridge smoothing removes material; it never increases radius. A small setting can work a corner without wiping the adjacent feature.Compare geometry before/after, not just glossy normals. Keep a deep notch after smoothing. Advancing with untouched roughness remains possible.
D05 · surfacesPaint colour follows contact along the axis and wraps around the turned form. Three mask styles reveal via touch coverage; separate optional decals place on the actual surface. Allow neutral timber and skipped decoration.Earlier bands persist; mask reveal changes only finish; decals do not enlarge geometry. Final screenshot/gallery reflects current player shape.
D06 · score/cashUse a declared geometric error measure with explicit undercut penalty, bounded 0–100. Choose/tune tolerance to the contour. Live preview and final meter share the function. Reward=max(30% quoted value, quoted value×score/100), rounded once.A target-perfect profile yields 100; untouched blank and deep notch do worse; painting alone changes neither. Result animation must end on stored values; credit once per completed-job ID before leaving results. Source scoring algorithm remains unknown.
D07 · reset/retryReset within craft confirms loss of current unsold work, reconstructs the same raw blank and clears finish. No cash penalty or reward; owned styles/workshop retained. Retry after settlement starts a new job ID with the same profile.No reward farming through reload/repeated Continue. Reset never partially restores a single cut. Back from results opens gallery/hub, not a duplicate sale.
D08 · earned purchasesCheck wallet before commit; one atomic debit + ownership/milestone update. Insufficient balance leaves state unchanged and names needed cash. Owned styles remain selectable; workshop max 10 then mastery loop.500 purchase from 873 leaves 373, milestone increments once. Rapid double tap/reload cannot double debit. No hidden cutting benefit.
D09 · presentationPortrait 390×844 first. Customer/brief above, lathe in middle, thumb tools/forward below safe area; stage name + contour thumbnail. Use translucent/quiet background behind contact, strong contour contrast and minimum 44 px controls.No scroll during a cut; no important UI under browser chrome/notch. Landscape letterboxes the play window while Settings remains usable. Avoid tiny text in live preview.
D10 · EN/RUIn-game Settings language switch EN/RU updates every menu, help, order, result, store, confirmation and accessibility label immediately; persist separately from progress. Numbers use consistent units.Switch during a partly painted job preserves geometry, tool, cash, stage and audio settings. Test longer Russian strings without clipping. This English report itself needs no language switch.
D11 · audio controlsIndependent Music and Effects sliders 0–100, touch minimum 44 px hit regions, visible numeric value, keyboard arrows. Persist both. Zero fully mutes its bus; do not alter the other. Master/platform mute multiplies both buses without replacing stored slider values.Music 0/Effects 80 still plays contact; Music 60/Effects 0 keeps score bed and silences tool/UI/celebration. Restore settings after reload. Pause suspends all loops; resume only after permitted gesture.
D12 · resilienceOne portable index.html, local assets embedded/generated, no external fonts/CDNs. Local save works without SDK/network. Platform saves/settings separate; a failed account read is an error, not an empty account.Offline, file://, sleep/wake and reload mid-job keep the base playable. No crash or silent overwrite on sync failure; use last confirmed/local progress with a clear sync status.

Feel targets: start chips only on effective removal; reduce them on already-empty space; keep their scale subordinate to the contour. Show clean exposed end-grain/material instead of a uniform disappearing block. Give sanding softer dust and changing local roughness; paint has a colour-matched mist; stencil reveals in touched regions. Evaluate after the player's commit, showing the actual object and outline together. Target input response must be immediate enough for precision on the tested phone; latency, frame budget and effect density are to be measured in the implementation rather than invented here.

Art, asset rights and sound event sheet

Original target art direction

Use warm pale wood, darker grain, cream/plaster background and a turquoise work mat. A clean side-on turning view maximises contour reading; a modest three-quarter finished-object view celebrates the surface. The workshop should feel like a tidy maker's bench, not a dense wall of purchasable props. Original stylised customers can be simple silhouettes and restrained reactions. Make a visible distinction between raw bark, fresh cut, smoothed timber and paint.

The editorial screenshots are study evidence, not reusable game assets. Source characters, logos, textures, creator footage and donor art have no established adaptation licence. No licensed ready asset bundle is supplied. Produce original procedural meshes/materials/icons and original commissioned/generated audio with confirmed reuse rights; keep a rights ledger. Source metal materials may become optional cosmetic finishes after the timber loop is solid; this does not imply measured metal physics. No paid service is activated for this specification.

Asset / statusRequired deliveryTest
Geometry/materials · Designed / missingOriginal profiles for all 30 commissions, free three chisel footprints, sponge, spray, masks/decals, ten workshopstates. Procedural grain and lighting acceptable.Every small shoulder/candle remains reachable; recognisable silhouette and clean contour on phone.
UI/customer art · Designed / missingOriginal stage/tool/settings icons, bilingual text, modest original customer reactions, gallery renders from recipes.No source screenshot/brand used as interactive asset; contrast and touch targets pass.
Audio · Designed approximation / missingSeparate original Music and Effects buses; generated/procedural effects permissible. No original source audio licensed or independently auditioned.Judge purposeful target feel; do not claim original timbre or exact rhythm.
Trigger / cue roleSource locator / confidenceDesigned target brief / readiness
Tool enters material / continuous contactA16–30s, B95s visual chips; source sound attributed, not independently heard.Short attack, woody granular scrape with gentle low motor layer; modulate by effective removal, not raw touch. Fade on release/empty space. Multiple variations avoid harsh repetition. Original cue missing.
Sponge contact / refineA172–190s, B149–160s; sponge interface checked; sound unverified.Quieter broad abrasive noise, soften as roughness decreases; no loud impacts. Start/stop with actual contact. Original cue missing.
Spray contact / colourA205–235s, Bpaintstage; finish states checked, sound unverified.Soft aerosol hiss with slight continuous variation; stop when no spray input. Colour change uses a low UI tick. Original cue missing.
Mask peel / revealB182s prompt checked; motion/sound not measured.Light paper peel fragments triggered by newly revealed coverage; no full-length loop if finger stops. Original cue missing.
Stage commit / evaluation / cashA248s, B192.096s/C807.128s checked results; timing and fanfare unverified.One modest success chime; sparse ticking during counted display; stop on stored total, no overlapping reward fanfares after doubleclick. UI cues highest intelligibility, celebration brief. Original cues missing.
Earned workshop/style purchaseB419→424s checked 500 debit; sound unverified.One gentle wood tap+bright confirmation, tied to successful commit only; denied action uses quiet neutral click, not punishment. Original cues missing.
Music / craft and hub contextNo original game music independently heard; creator soundtrack cannot establish source score.Original gentle plucked/soft mallet bed with sparse sustained harmony; steady low-density pulse, no asserted BPM. Loop seamlessly; lower energy during cutting, a small lift on result, then settle. Music optional and default modest; no loop seam or forced fanfare after mute. Original music missing.

Use short perceptual response and fades without pretending measured source milliseconds. Contact cues stop with input readiness; modal, pause, reset and blur silence them. Duck the music slightly for result confirmation if both buses are active; effects 0 must not duck music for inaudible cues. No spatial stereo positioning is required for a centred single object. Validate on phone speakers and headphones after obtaining original assets.

bug.games platform plan · Designed

Current SDK reference was checked 06 Oct 2026. Implementation must recheck it before writing integration code. The game's core runs without the platform. Guard import of /sdk/bloomplay.js on the game origin; distinguish absent SDK in an offline build from a failed initialization. Use native gameplay, analytics and progress APIs; no third-party analytics or fabricated watch-ad controls.

Measurement that answers a design question

Call gameplayStart() when a commission becomes interactive and gameplayStop() at pause/results/hub/blur as appropriate, restoring on actual play. Do not duplicate automatic page-view/gameplay events. Use analytics.track(event,props) only at the triggers below; no personal data, per-frame pointer stream or inferred income.

Event / exact triggerMinimal propertiesQuestion
first_contact · first effective removal once per new saveprofile_family, tool_profile, active_seconds_from_job_startDoes the player understand the first action? Active elapsed time excludes background/modal pauses.
stage_commit · explicit advance from craft stagejob_id, stage, active_seconds, coverage_bucket, score_previewWhere do players move on without effective work? No geometry payload.
undercut_first · first material removal inside target per jobprofile_family, tool_profile, stage, depth_bucketWhich feature/tool produces the first damaging error? Bucket severity, not each stroke.
job_reset · confirmed free reset before settlementprofile_family, stage, score_preview, active_secondsDoes damage become abandonment or an intentional new attempt?
job_settled · after atomic once-only creditjob_id, profile_family, score, quoted_max, payout, attempt_indexDoes score/reward support improvement across repeated shapes? Counts are not revenue.
earned_purchase · successful soft-cash debitcategory, item_id, cost, milestone, balance_bucketDo players choose visible workshop growth or styles? No duplicate event on restored save.
settings_change · committed language/slider changesetting, value_bucket, stageAre audio and language controls discoverable? Debounce a slider to pointer release/keyboard completion.
resume_job · saved unfinished job becomes interactivestage, profile_family, local_or_platformDoes job continuity work? No device identity or account identifier.
Declared momentExact first reach trigger
First clean contactFirst effective cut in any job; once per save.
First finished objectFirst persisted settlement, including imperfect craft.
First workshop upgradeFirst committed workshop milestone.
A narrow neckFirst settlement of a neck-bearing profile at ≥85% target score.
A personal finishFirst settled object with at least two paint bands or a pattern/decal.
The layered cakeFirst settled cake; perfection not required.
Workshop completeMilestone 10 committed; mastery loop stays playable.

Report these exact names through progress.moment(name) once at their stated trigger. The listed order is the expected teaching order; keep game actions free if a player reaches another milestone early. Store reached flags without blocking gameplay when offline; use a local diagnostic log outside the platform. Settings belong to their own save key; use SDK save/cache facilities instead of replacing a failed remote read with a fresh account.

Extras: none at launch

The full 30 commissions, ten milestones, all functional tools, defined styles, gallery and endless loop are free. products:[]; render no empty Extras screen. A future original lathe-finish set could add purely cosmetic bench materials beyond this base. It is currently unbuilt/unavailable, has no live price, belongs outside products, and is not promised as an available purchase.

If such a set is later completed, tested and separately submitted for review, discover it from the normal bench customisation screen. A temporary try-on reverts on exit and grants no ownership; performance, score and cash stay identical. Show a buy button only for an actually sellable product returned by monetization.getProducts(), at its returned price. Confirm durable ownership via getEntitlements() after purchase(id); grant once. Confirmed ownership outranks catalogue availability. Empty successful catalogue means unavailable, not an explained cause; service failure means temporarily unavailable; offline means no transaction. A failed ownership read never revokes last-confirmed ownership.

Future purchase checks must cover owned, sellable, absent, offline, error, cancellation and insufficient coins; restore audio/input after the platform sheet. Current SDK documents platform coins without top-ups, not an ad API or creator payout. No financial revenue model or ad dependency is inferred. Live publication and product review are separate later actions.

Acceptance cases and design-space tests

Run these on the ordinary game build with actual touch/mouse inputs. Debug profile injection can test numerical boundaries separately; it does not validate normal control or balance.

Case / setupReal input → expected resultRule / status
01 · raw arrow, flat chiselDrag once through an outer band → only contacted region shrinks, chips appear, outline remains. Move in empty space → no further removal cue.R01/D01/D02; source contact checked, target mapping Designed.
02 · same raw blank and pathRepeat path with flat, round, point on fresh blanks → distinct footprints; free narrow tool can reach shoulder/candle.R02/D02; footprints require implemented verification.
03 · deliberate deep notchCut through contour, advance, sand, paint, reveal → notch persists; final score below perfect, live preview agrees.R03/R04 unverified source restoration; D03–D06 Designed invariant.
04 · rough adjacent shoulderSet small then large sponge width; drag locally → width changes effect, uncontacted spans remain; radius never increases.R04 slider checked, D04 Designed.
05 · half-painted objectApply two bands and pattern, place decal; choose skip options on another job → actual carved shape survives, bare finish allowed, no geometric score change.R05 visual state checked, D05/D06 Designed.
06 · result count-upWait through animation → one stored accuracy/reward; repeated Continue and reload do not pay again. Compare wallet before/after.R06/R07 local examples; D06 Designed ledger.
07 · first arrow from cash 0Finish at 100% → quoted max 300, payout 300, cash 300; second clean arrow → cash 600, upgrade 500 leaves 100.Designed economy; original arrow 300 checked, but target pathway is not source proof.
08 · workshop cash 873, milestone 0Tap upgrade 500 once and again rapidly → cash 373, milestone 1, next 578, one visible bench change.R09 checked instance; D08 Designed atomicity.
09 · cash below unlock costTap style/upgrade → clear needed-cash feedback, no debit/no item. Then earn enough and buy → one debit, persistent owned item.Source refusal unknown; D08 Designed.
10 · halfway carved jobConfirm Reset → raw same target, finish cleared, cash/owned items retained, no credit. Reload after a later partial job → resume geometry/stage.Source reset retention unknown; D07/D12 Designed.
11 · first/new playerUse guide without help page → first effective contact dismisses it; job two has no repeated guide and same manual controls.Local pilot transfer Designed; no engagement metric claimed.
12 · Russian during paintingSwitch EN→RU→reload → translated labels fit, job, cash, paint and selected tool intact.D10 target requirement.
13 · audio isolationMusic 0/Effects 80 then Music 60/Effects 0; reload → independent buses and stored values; pause releases loops.D11; source audio unknown.
14 · phone 390×844, landscape, blurDrag near edges, rotate device, open Settings, pointer cancel → no stuck cut/scroll, no UI overlap, tool remains discoverable.D01/D09; measure real-device responsiveness.
15 · complete free gameOrdinary play reaches all 30 commission variants, all free collection items, all ten milestones and repeating mastery. Cake reachable without purchase.Target scope Designed; not a source ending reconstruction.
16 · offline/file and SDK failureOpen without network or simulate failed SDK initialization → complete base works, local resume survives, no Extras button, no fake ad. Platform save error never overwrites confirmed remote state.D12/platform plan Designed; preview integration still needed later.
17 · ordinary event auditPlay first two jobs, reset one, buy first bench → each custom event/moment fires once at declared trigger; no automatic page/gameplay duplicates.Platform plan; logging only until implementation.
18 · three source episodesInspect B 100% / 300 stable, A 99% / 279 and A 92% / 257 plus the 873→373 purchase; compare captions/rule components to extracted figures.Semantic receiving check, not a requirement to replicate unverified source formula.
19 · previous player issuesComplete narrow ends; check busy bench contrast; read upgrade promise before buying → no unreachable authored feature, no outline obscuration, no false functional benefit.Dated anecdote converted to target test; shipped source fix unknown.

Separate fidelity limits: no original game audio independently heard; no verified REPAIR execution or source reset persistence; no exact shape-score, pay or shop-randomness formula; no complete source catalogue, rank cap or ending; build numbers unknown. Additional stills resolve selected interfaces and values, not those mechanisms. The complete target is implementable by explicit design choices; a future built game's feel and balance still require real inputs and phone tests.

Embedded evidence index and receiving procedure

Every indexed image below is embedded in this HTML. Source-player pixels were cropped to the game area; gameplay was not generated or repainted. Click any figure, or focus it and press Enter/Space; use View 1:1 to read small values with touch scrolling. Exact locators belong here rather than in editorial captions. Source A/B contexts stay separate.

Receiving agent: parse the document with an HTML parser; extract the full authored text including details, tables and captions without serialising image base 64 into text. Resolve the exact required figure IDs, decode each image and open it with an image-capable tool. Check the contact, stable reward and benchpurchase pairs before coding. Extraction is internal; the user transfers only this HTML. If the receiving environment cannot inspect images, state that limitation rather than claiming fidelity.
